questions.q: What is Azure Blob storage's namespace, technically?
options: Flat — every object is a key inside a container, and 'folders' are just naming conventions using slashes
A true hierarchical file system with real folders by default
A relational database table structure
A queue-based message system
questions.explain: A blob name containing slashes looks like a folder path, but there's no real directory object behind it in plain Blob storage.

options: Blob storage with the hierarchical namespace feature enabled — not a separate storage product
A completely separate Azure service unrelated to Blob storage
A type of virtual machine for big data workloads
A managed SQL database for analytics
questions.explain: One setting, turned on at account creation, is the entire difference between plain Blob storage and ADLS Gen2.

questions.q: What does enabling hierarchical namespace actually change?
options: Directories become real entries in the storage account's index, enabling atomic directory operations and true file/directory semantics
It changes the storage account's pricing tier automatically
It converts all existing blobs into a SQL table
It has no functional effect, only a cosmetic one
questions.explain: With hierarchical namespace on, a directory is a real object, not just a naming pattern.

questions.q: Why is renaming a directory slower on plain Blob storage than on ADLS Gen2?
options: Without a real directory object, the storage service must individually rewrite every blob whose name started with that prefix
Blob storage doesn't allow renaming at all under any circumstances
ADLS Gen2 doesn't support renaming directories either
Renaming speed is identical between the two
questions.explain: A true directory rename in ADLS Gen2 is one atomic operation; on plain Blob storage, it requires rewriting every matching blob.

questions.q: Can hierarchical namespace be turned on after a storage account has already been created?
options: No — it must be decided at creation time, not changed later
Yes, at any time from the account's settings blade
Yes, but only by Microsoft support
It's enabled automatically after 30 days
questions.explain: This is a creation-time decision, which is why it's worth understanding clearly before creating a real storage account.
